deep.reconstruction:
The page is a draft (Konzept) of a letter from Riemann to Dedekind. It is not a mathematical computation sheet. It has three parts.

(1) Personal opening. Riemann says that in the unrest of the coming journey he could not keep his promise to write to Dedekind in Zürich. He would anyway have written only a few lines if there had been a prospect of their meeting on the journey. Dedekind was at the ETH Zürich from 1858 to 1862, which dates the letter to 1858-62, probably around one of Riemann's journeys (for example 1862). This dating is my inference.

(2) A note for the typesetter or for whoever reads the first proof. The determinant notation on the reverse side ('umstehende Bezeichnung der Determinante') was chosen only to make the formulas easier to print. If the type is not in stock ('nicht vorräthig'), the printer should either use single brackets instead of the double ones, or suppress the note on the reverse and keep the earlier notation. So Dedekind was evidently seeing a Riemann paper through the press, and that paper contained determinants written with a special bracket notation.

(3) Several crossed-out and restarted versions of one key sentence. Riemann is evidently drafting a corrected passage for that paper. Its content in modern terms:

Let E(z_1,...,z_p) be an expression that is symmetric in the quantities (points) z_1,...,z_p.
- As a function of any single z_ν, with the others fixed, E is an algebraic function. That is, it is a single-valued meromorphic function on the Riemann surface (the compact algebraic curve) of the underlying equation.
- The points z_ν at which E becomes infinitely large or infinitely small (its poles and zeros) do not depend on the other z's.
- Riemann wants to conclude: 'Es ist daher gleich einer von den Größen z unabhängigen Größe', i.e. E is a constant.

The second draft makes the logic explicit. Because E is symmetric, it suffices to argue for one arbitrary z_ν, say z_2 in the first draft.

Implicit steps (mine):
- Either E has no zeros or poles at all as a function of z_ν (e.g. E is a quotient in which they cancel). Then by Liouville's theorem on a compact Riemann surface, E is constant in z_ν.
- Or its divisor in z_ν is a fixed divisor D independent of the other z's. Then E = c(z_1,...,ẑ_ν,...,z_p)·f(z_ν), with f a fixed function having divisor D. Applying this to every variable via symmetry, and normalising, gives the conclusion that E is independent of all the z's.

The abandoned word 'Factor' (replaced by 'Größe') shows that Riemann first wrote 'equal to a factor independent of the z' and then sharpened it.

The page ends with the bibliographic jotting 'Monatsberichte 1846 1850', presumably the Berlin Academy Monatsberichte, cited as a reference for the paper.
errors: As literally written, the argument is incomplete. A function on a compact Riemann surface with prescribed zeros and poles is determined only up to a constant factor. So 'zeros/poles independent of the other z' gives E = c(other z)·f(z_ν), not yet a constant. Constancy follows only if the zeros and poles cancel (no divisor) or after normalisation together with the symmetry argument. Riemann's own crossing-out of 'Factor' and repeated restarts suggest he was working on exactly this formulation.
The first draft says 'durch eine algebraische Function von z_2' without completing the clause (the verb is missing). This is a drafting slip, not a mathematical error.

results.what: A symmetric expression in points z_1..z_p that is an algebraic (meromorphic) function of each z_ν, with zeros/poles in z_ν independent of the other points, is a constant.
results.modern_name: Liouville's theorem on compact Riemann surfaces (a meromorphic function without poles is constant; a function is determined by its divisor up to a constant), applied to symmetric functions of divisors
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen 1857; Über das Verschwinden der Theta-Functionen 1865), building on Liouville/Abel

results.what: Special bracket notation for determinants proposed for printing, with instructions to the typesetter.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a letter draft showing Dedekind assisting with proofs of a Riemann paper, plus a standard Riemann-style Liouville/symmetry argument. It is of biographical and editorial interest (dating, the Riemann–Dedekind collaboration) but contains no new mathematics.

checkable.asserts: Toy example: a symmetric quotient of alternating determinants whose zeros cancel is constant (independent of z1, z2).
Vandermonde ratio: symmetric in z1, z2, z3, no zeros or poles left, hence a constant.

transcription_corrections: In the typesetter note, 'statt der doppelten' is an interlinear insertion above the crossed-out word before 'Klammern'. The phrase reads 'entweder statt der doppelten [einfache] Klammern zu setzen'.

First mathematical draft: 'und die Werthe von z_2 für welche er unendlich groß und unendlich klein wird sind von den Größen z unabhängig'. The insertion above the struck line is 'eine symmetrische Function der Größen z ist'.
In the final sentence of the first draft, 'Factor' is struck and 'Größe' is written above: 'gleich einer von den Größen z unabhängigen Größe'.
Second draft: 'Da der Ausdruck eine symmetrische F. d. Größen z ist, so gilt derselbe [struck: in Bezug auf jedes] beliebige z_ν'. The phrase 'jedes beliebige' is partly struck.
